messages:
jack (support): heads-up: Customer ACME reports p95/p99 spikes for Dedicated pool dp-7 over last 30m, several 504s. They say it started after a traffic burst at ~17:10 UTC.
maria (sre): saw alerts. p95 jumped from 210ms -> 1.2s and p99 to 3.8s. Provisioner queue length increased and stayed high. Any recent deploys? @alan?
alan (runtime): no code deploys in the last hour from runtime. There was a config change to autoscale window earlier today (lowered ramp delay). Could be interacting badly with bursty load.
sophia (oncall): attaching customer traces now. Jack, can you paste the curl that reproduces the timeout? I want a concrete repro for load test.
jack (support): customer shared this script:

```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

They ran it across ~10 clients concurrently.
maria (sre): good. I pulled provisioner logs for dp-7:

```
2026-03-15T17:11:05Z provisioner[dp-7] queue_size=42 attach_attempts=5 warmup_in_progress=true
2026-03-15T17:11:18Z provisioner[dp-7] attach_error=timeout backoff=10s
2026-03-15T17:12:40Z provisioner[dp-7] queue_size=68 attach_attempts=12 warmup=false
```

Looks like many attach attempts failing due to cold start/warmup timing out, queue grows and requests time out at API layer.
alan (runtime): logs show GPU nodes are created but zapper (node init) takes 90-120s before the runtime process is ready. Our attach timeout is 60s currently.
sophia (oncall): scale-bot: give me dp-7 metrics snapshot.
scale-bot: dp-7 cpu=85% gpu=96% warm_instances=2 desired_instances=12 attaching=6 queue=71 p95=1200ms p99=3800ms
jack (support): customer says sometimes requests return 500 with message "no available workers" before timeout.
maria (sre): probable flow: burst -> autoscaler triggers new nodes -> node creation + image pull + runtime init > attach timeout -> provisioner retries -> queue grows -> API returns timeouts/500s when queue hits max.
alan (runtime): quick mitigation options:
- increase attach timeout to 180s (runtime config) to allow warmups to finish
- reduce aggressiveness of clients with rate limit advice
- add short-term fallback routing to cached/quantized smaller model variant
- increase pool minimum to keep more warm instances (costly)

Which should we do now? I'm ready to flip config if we agree.
sophia (oncall): priority is to stop customer errors ASAP. Jack, tell customer we'll do a hot rollback: increase attach timeout and add emergency fallback routing. Can we do both within 10-15m?
jack (support): I'll message them. They prefer latency over errors, so fallback to smaller model is OK.
maria (sre): I'll open incident and run a controlled change. Proposed steps:
1) set runtime.attach_timeout=180s for dp-7
2) bump dp-7 min_replicas from 2 -> 6
3) add route override for ACME to model redwood-small-quant as a fallback when queue > 30
4) monitor p95/p99 and queue

I can push 1 and 3 quickly, 2 requires provisioning which will take additional time.
alan (runtime): pushing attach_timeout now. Command:

```
redctl pool update dp-7 --set runtime.attach_timeout=180
```

I'll watch logs.
scale-bot: change queued: runtime.attach_timeout -> 180 for dp-7 by alan
alan (runtime): logs after change:

```
2026-03-15T17:18:02Z provisioner[dp-7] attach_attempts=3 attach_timeout=180 node_ready=true
2026-03-15T17:18:35Z provisioner[dp-7] attaching=4 queue_size=28
```

queue size started trending down.
sophia (oncall): jack, let customer know we increased attach timeout. Also we can enable fallback routing now.
jack (support): messaged them: "We increased attach timeout and added a fallback to redwood-small-quant for your traffic if we detect worker starvation. Monitoring closely." They replied :thumbsup: and asked for ETA on full resolution.
maria (sre): I pushed route override for customer ACME:

```
redctl route override --customer acme --when "pool_queue > 30" --to-model redwood-small-quant
```

scale-bot: route override applied for customer acme
alan (runtime): I'm also kicking off a warmup job to pre-pull images and start runtime processes on 4 new nodes to catch up faster.

```
redctl pool prewarm dp-7 --count 4 --image-pull=true --start-runtime=true
```

scale-bot: prewarm job started id=prewarm-917
sophia (oncall): good. Maria, what's the immediate metric delta? p95/p99?
maria (sre): after changes p95 -> 320ms, p99 -> 620ms, queue -> 10. Errors dropped to near zero. Customer reports latency improved significantly.
jack (support): customer: "latency much better, saw a few slow requests but most healthy. Thanks." they asked for a postmortem and a permanent fix.
maria (sre): immediate mitigations worked. Next steps for durable fix:
- increase default attach_timeout for Dedicated pools from 60 -> 120s while we optimize zapper init
- implement proactive prewarm heuristics for sudden bursts (detect increasing RPS and start nodes earlier)
- add a short randomized backoff & jitter to attach retry logic to avoid thundering herd
- revisit autoscaler ramp policy (maybe increase scale-up rate and smoothing window)
- improve observability: surface attaching count in Console per-pool

I'll create a GH issue with owners. Alan, will runtime team own attach timeout change and zapper perf work? Jack, can you coordinate customer PM and share postmortem link?
alan (runtime): yes, we'll own zapper optimization and a config rollout for default attach_timeout.
jack (support): will do. I'll schedule a customer call tomorrow and send an incident summary.
sophia (oncall): closing this thread after incident doc posted. Add links here when available.
maria (sre): opening incident: INC-2026-03-15-001 assigned to maria/alan/jack
scale-bot: incident INC-2026-03-15-001 created (severity=high)
